scope: Fresh current-source post-QPSG paired SQLite comparison against original 0.4. This is performance evidence, not a performance exception or release acceptance.
summary: Earlier warm-replay and exact-retry regressions are not observed above their thresholds in this current-source run. All historical findings remain retained. New/sustained flags remain open for small-history reopen and append-tail latency.

conditions.purpose: Post-QPSG candidate SQLite performance review against original 0.4.0.
conditions.order: Alternating before/after and after/before pairs; warmup pair retained but excluded.
conditions.storage: Same NVMe/Btrfs data parent; SQLite WAL/FULL; OS cache uncontrolled; no fsync bypass.
conditions.concurrent_work: Do not overlap the pinned full chaos campaign or another benchmark on CPU 4.

limits: Medians summarize run-level quantiles; they are not pooled event percentiles.
A bootstrap interval does not waive a sustained performance review flag.
The fixture has unchanged data and benchmark source; cache and shared-host effects remain uncontrolled.
There are only ten replay observations per process; sixteen-record append has fourteen observations, so its nearest-rank p95 is the maximum. Run medians do not establish a rare-tail guarantee.
No concurrent qualification or benchmark was launched during these measured processes; this remains a shared host with uncontrolled frequency, OS cache and external activity.
The preflight rejects tracked candidate changes. All per-run tracked diffs are empty; post-run git-content and resolved-build-content inventories include symlink targets.
The previous 16 SQLite flags are not erased or accepted. A later unflagged run is a scoped observation, not a waiver of the two remaining flags or a proof of equivalence.
Full immutable-source chaos was deliberately not run at the user's request. This timing comparison does not close that gate.
